quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden movements.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, use both brakes when you need to stop, slow down, and avoid sudden movements. Watch out for oily spots, shaded areas, dirt, gravel, and bridges. These surfaces have less grip than normal roads.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow all rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down. Use both brakes when you stop and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.
Only partially cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Wear jackets and pants that cover your arms and legs completely. They should fit snug but allow you to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection in a crash.

questions.question: The front brake is:

options.text: Only for use if the rear brake fails.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safe when used correctly.
questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used correctly. It provides more than three-fourths of your total stopping power.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Can greatly reduce serious head injuries.
Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can greatly reduce serious head injuries.
questions.explanation: Wearing a DOT-approved helmet greatly improves your chances of avoiding serious head or neck injury in a crash. It will not limit your side vision.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) are designed to:

options.text: Prevent brakes from working on dry roads.
Tell you when brake pads need replacing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop skidding and wheel lock-up.
questions.explanation: ABS stops skidding and wheel lock-up during hard braking. It works by releasing and re-applying brake pressure to keep wheels from locking up and maintain maximum stopping power.

questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift down one gear at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: Shift down one gear at a time. Ease out the clutch gradually between each gear shift.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of a crash, you should:

options.text: Make yourself visible to other drivers.
Keep other drivers guessing about your plans.
Always stay very close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make yourself visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show other drivers what you plan to do. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
Ask other friends to convince them not to ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask other friends to convince them not to ride.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has been drinking to ride. Stop them from riding by any means possible. Get a group of friends to talk to them and pressure them not to ride.

questions.question: A cushion of space while riding helps you:

options.text: Have time to react to hazards.
Avoid being able to maneuver safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have time to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: A cushion of space around your motorcycle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
Have only one set of footrests.
Not ask the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Never carry a passenger unless your motorcycle has a seat for two riders. Your motorcycle must have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear as you do.

questions.question: Goggles will:

options.text: Work as well as a face shield.
Protect as much as a windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect only your eyes.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield protects your whole face and is better than goggles. A windshield is not enough protection by itself.

questions.question: Waiting one hour after one drink before riding:

options.text: Means you cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Means alcohol will not affect your riding skills.
Is fine as long as you ride slowly.
May not completely remove alcohol from your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not completely remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: On average, your body can eliminate one drink per hour. The time needed to lower your blood alcohol content varies, so the safest choice is not to ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Not check your rearview mirrors for traffic behind you.
Look for chances to squeeze through stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well back from the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or if another vehicle comes too fast from behind.

questions.question: Your best source for information about your motorcycle is:
questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Use your owner's manual for information about your specific motorcycle. It explains how your motorcycle works and what maintenance it needs.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have which types of brakes?
questions.correctAnswerText: Front and rear
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.

questions.question: Even if your turn seems obvious, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Only need a turn signal if pedestrians are near.
Only need a turn signal at stop lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when you turn or change lanes, even if you think it is obvious. Other vehicles may be nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually:
questions.correctAnswerText: Made of leather.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are typically made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may pull out suddenly into your path.
Other drivers may be moving slowly while looking for a spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may pull out suddenly into your path.
questions.explanation: A driver may pull out of a parking space without looking and hit you. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out from between parked cars.

questions.question: What should you do when riding a motorcycle you don't know?

options.text: Test the seat to make sure it is comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good condition.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
Ride normally because most bikes are the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different. Learn how the new motorcycle works before you ride it. Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes to understand how they feel on this bike.

questions.question: What happens when you take a corner too fast?

options.text: You may cross into another lane.
It is better than going too slowly.
You will usually stay in your lane.
It is okay because motorcycles are small.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or go off the road. Slow down before you turn.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about hazards or changes in road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What happens if your motorcycle's chain or belt breaks?

options.text: Power to the rear wheel suddenly increases.
Power to the rear wheel suddenly stops.
Power to the front wheel suddenly stops.
Power to the front wheel suddenly increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Power to the rear wheel suddenly stops.
questions.explanation: If your drive chain or belt breaks, the rear wheel loses power immediately.
